citations.narrative:
During the offloading of Flight 786, a dog kennel was improperly positioned near the platform end of the operating
conveyor belt. A large suitcase placed above the kennel moved down the belt and struck the kennel, causing it to fall
approximately three feet to the ground. The kennel sustained damage. The dog inside was immediately inspected by the
ramp agent and showed no visible external injuries. At the time of the incident, the ramp agent assigned to the belt had
moved away from the end of the conveyor. Lack of proper attention to live animals on or near conveyor equipment poses
significant risks, including stress, injury, or escape.
The registrant must ensure that the primary enclosures are not placed on inclined conveyor ramps used to load and
unload aircraft unless an attendant is present at each end of the conveyor belt. The issue was identified by the
intermediate handler, and corrective actions along with coaching were provided to the ramp agents involved prior to
today’s inspection.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the manager and the airline representative.
